advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack against a vacuous pass by asserting `_HEAVY` is non-empty (e.g. `assert _HEAVY`) before the clean-runtime subprocess check.
evidence: tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py:68-70 `heavy = {_HEAVY!r}` ... `leaked = [module for module in heavy if module in sys.modules]` ... `print("LEAK:"... if leaked else "CLEAN")`

tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py:75 `assert cp.stdout.strip() == "CLEAN"` — with `_HEAVY == ()` this is satisfied regardless of what the runtime imports (the oracle re-derives its subject from the same file the production rule reads, so one deletion disables both the ruff rule and this test's ability to catch it).
advisory.finding: test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack now derives its check set `_HEAVY` from the same pyproject.toml banned-module-level-imports list the TID253 rule reads, so emptying or shrinking that list makes the test pass vacuously (empty `heavy` -> empty `leaked` -> prints 'CLEAN') instead of failing — the one surviving behavioral test cannot detect the heavy-stack-laziness contract being disabled.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert _HEAVY, "banned-module-level-imports is empty — the single-source read is broken or the list was silently cleared"` immediately after _HEAVY is built, so an emptied/shrunk pyproject list fails the test loudly rather than passing CLEAN.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a ratchet in test_ruff_ratchet.py asserting `TID251` and `TID253` are in `_ruff_select()` and that banned-module-level-imports / the banned-api `tests` entry are non-empty, mirroring the ASYNC/DTZ/RUF/PLW1510 guards.
evidence: Added config this diff relies on: pyproject.toml `+    "TID251",` / `+    "TID253",` in select and the `+[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]` banned lists.

test_ruff_ratchet.py guards every comparable family with an explicit select-membership ratchet: `:48-49` ASYNC, `:52-53` DTZ, `:56-59` RUF, `:152-154` PLW1510, `:157-165` the PT subset in both directions — but no TID251/TID253 assertion exists.

ABSENCE rationale: the two deleted AST scans (test_no_core_module_imports_heavy_stack_at_module_scope, test_no_tests_rooted_imports_anywhere_under_tests) were the regression guards for these contracts; after the fold the sole guard is config added in this same diff, and search of test_ruff_ratchet.py shows no reference to TID251/TID253 or banned-module-level-imports.
blocking.finding: This diff folds two deleted behavioral contracts entirely into ruff TID251/TID253 but adds no ratchet asserting those codes remain in `[tool.ruff.lint].select` or that the banned lists stay populated — unlike every comparable rule family in test_ruff_ratchet.py — so a later edit that drops TID251/TID253 or empties banned-module-level-imports / the banned-api `tests` entry would silently delete the a371 and heavy-stack-laziness contracts on a green build.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add `assert "TID251" in _ruff_select()` and `assert "TID253" in _ruff_select()`, plus a check that `[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports].banned-module-level-imports` is non-empty and contains the heavy stacks and that `banned-api` has the `tests` key, so a config removal fails the suite rather than silently dropping the contract.
